title: Perf-canary integration for provisioning readiness (minimal throughput/latency gate before Ready)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
description:
Context
- We’re adding automated readiness gates to the Dedicated provision-to-ready pipeline. Smoke tests + health checks catch obvious failures, but we still have cases where a pool “looks healthy” yet has materially worse throughput/latency (driver mismatch, wrong runtime chart values, MIG config drift, kernel params, etc.).
- This issue integrates perf-canary as the final step of Validating: run a lightweight benchmark (“readiness suite”) against the newly bootstrapped pool before transitioning to Ready.

Goal
- Gate Ready on a minimal performance signal that:
  1) confirms the dataplane can serve tokens end-to-end
  2) catches obvious perf regressions (misconfig, wrong image/runtime, missing optimizations)
  3) is fast enough to keep time-to-ready targets

Scope
- Add a new provisioning validation sub-step: perf-canary readiness suite.
- Implement orchestration in fleet-provisioner/control plane to schedule the run, fetch results, and write pass/fail + summary to the provisioning run record.
- Define default thresholds + per-SKU overrides, with conservative initial values and a plan to tighten post-pilot.
- Emit stage events/metrics for canary duration and outcome.

Non-goals
- Full benchmark coverage (long-run soak, multiple models, or quality evals).
- Runtime-level optimization work.

Proposed behavior
- When a run reaches stage=Validating, fleet-provisioner triggers perf-canary readiness mode:
  - launched as a Kubernetes Job inside the new pool cluster (so we validate intra-cluster networking + service discovery)
  - hits the pool’s inference endpoint using internal DNS/service VIP (same path used by routing, minus global routing advertisement)
  - uses a fixed small prompt set and concurrency meant to approximate “is it basically working and not wildly slow”
  - writes results JSON to object storage + posts a compact summary back to control plane

Benchmark spec (initial)
- Suite: perf-canary “readiness” mode (see perf-canary PR-287).
- Model:
  - Default: the pool’s configured default model (if already pulled/available), else fallback to a pinned lightweight verification model.
  - For pilot we will prefer the pool default (to detect mismatched runtime flags for that arch).
- Traffic shape (defaults):
  - Warmup: 60s
  - Measure: 120s
  - Concurrency: 4 (tunable per SKU)
  - Prompt mix: small fixed set; output tokens capped (to reduce runtime)
- Output: JSON summary with at least:
  - pass/fail
  - throughput tokens/sec
  - p50/p95 TTFT (time-to-first-token)
  - p50/p95 inter-token latency
  - error rate and top error (if any)
  - metadata: sku/region, runtime version, chart version, image version

Thresholds (initial, conservative)
- Pass if ALL are true:
  - error_rate <= 0.5%
  - p95_ttft_ms <= sku_default.p95_ttft_ms
  - tokens_per_sec >= sku_default.min_tps
- Threshold source of truth:
  - ship defaults keyed by sku class (e.g., A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S) + model family (where needed)
  - allow pool config override (validated via schema) for:
    - min_tps
    - p95_ttft_ms
    - max_duration_minutes
  - overrides must be recorded in audit trail; break-glass overrides handled by separate control (ENG-2751), not this ticket.

State machine + gating semantics
- perf-canary is a hard gate for Ready.
- If perf-canary fails:
  - provisioning run moves to Failed (or stays in Validating with terminal failure reason), with a structured error code and the canary summary attached.
  - capacity must not be advertised to routing.
- Retry semantics:
  - “transient” failures (Job scheduling, image pull, canary infra) should be retried with bounded backoff.
  - “performance threshold” failures should not auto-retry more than once (to avoid burning time); require operator intervention or explicit re-run.

Implementation plan
1) Orchestration
- Add control-plane/fleet-provisioner action: TriggerPerfCanary(run_id, pool_id, config)
- Create K8s Job spec template with:
  - perf-canary container image tag pinned
  - env vars for endpoint URL, auth token (scoped), suite params
  - resource requests/limits appropriate to avoid starving the node
  - timeoutSecondsAfterFinished set for cleanup

2) Result ingestion
- perf-canary readiness suite writes:
  - /outputs/summary.json (required)
  - /outputs/raw.json (optional)
- Job uploads summary.json to object storage; posts a callback to control plane with location + checksum.
- Control plane persists:
  - canary_status: PASS/FAIL/ERROR
  - canary_summary_url
  - canary_metrics: flattened key/value fields in provisioning run record (for dashboards)

3) Metrics/Events
- Emit:
  - provisioning_stage_duration{stage="perf_canary"}
  - perf_canary_outcome{outcome, sku, region, model}
  - perf_canary_latency_ms (p50/p95)
  - perf_canary_tps
- Ensure cardinality safeguards (pool_id as exemplar/correlation only).

4) Operator UX
- CLI prints:
  - perf-canary outcome
  - reason (threshold breached or infra error)
  - link to summary.json and dashboard panel
- Re-run support via CLI stage rerun (ENG-2750 / ENG-2747 integration): allow rerun of perf-canary only if stage>=Validating.

Acceptance criteria
- A provisioning run cannot transition to Ready unless perf-canary outcome=PASS.
- perf-canary completes within 5 minutes (p95) on pilot SKUs under normal conditions.
- On failure, operators can see:
  - which metric breached
  - canary summary link
  - recommended runbook next step (e.g., check runtime chart versions, node driver, GPU health)
- Metrics are available for dashboarding (time-to-ready breakdown includes perf-canary).

Testing plan
- Unit: parse/validate canary summary JSON; threshold comparison logic; error classification.
- Integration (staging):
  - success path on internal staging pool
  - forced failure by setting min_tps absurdly high
  - infra failure by blocking Job from scheduling (taints) and confirming retry behavior
- Regression: ensure routing integration only consumes Ready (ENG-2759).

Rollout notes
- Behind provisioning pipeline feature flag in staging first.
- Start with conservative thresholds and log-only comparison for 2-3 runs (but still require PASS; thresholds set low enough to not block normal pools).
- Tighten thresholds after baseline collection (tracked in follow-up).

Links
- GitHub: perf-canary PR-287 (readiness suite mode)
- Related control-plane work: PR-48234 (Ready gating in routing), PR-48245 (fix race: Ready set before perf-canary completion)
- Related Linear: ENG-2746 (readiness gates), ENG-2748 (stage timing metrics/events)

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should Validating capacity be usable for customer traffic? A: No; routing only uses Ready.
- Q: Per-SKU thresholds or global? A: Per-SKU defaults with optional per-pool override (schema-validated).
comments: 2025-02-21 (Rina Kobayashi): Sync with Rafael/Aisha: we want this to be a hard gate, but keep the suite <=5m p95. I’ll start with warmup=60s measure=120s, concurrency=4 and adjust after first staging run.

2025-02-24 (Ethan Park): Please make sure we don’t mark Ready until canary callback is persisted. We had an earlier incident where Validating completed on smoke tests and routing picked up capacity too early; gate needs to be transactional with state machine.

2025-02-27 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented Job launcher + result parser in fleet-provisioner. Added error classification: THRESHOLD_BREACH vs JOB_FAILED vs TIMEOUT. Need help from Logan/Caleb to confirm metric names align with time-to-ready dashboard spec.

2025-03-01 (Rafael Mendes): First staging run failed with DNS misconfig; canary caught it (couldn’t resolve service endpoint) which is good. Confirmed it surfaces as JOB_FAILED with actionable message + link to runbook section. Retried after fixing CoreDNS and it passed.

2025-03-05 (Vanessa Ortiz): We should store the canary summary in the provisioning run record (URL + a few fields) so CS can reference “validated” in customer comms. Please include runtime/image/chart versions in summary if perf-canary can output it.

2025-03-07 (Rina Kobayashi): perf-canary readiness suite updated to include runtime/chart/image metadata in summary. Control plane stores flattened fields for dashboard filters. Added CLI output: shows breached metric and threshold values.

2025-03-10 (Miles Thornton): Multi-region note: allow a slightly higher TTFT threshold in eu-west due to cross-AZ LB variance during canary? Rina: we’re running in-cluster to avoid cross-region/LB noise; TTFT threshold is keyed by sku, not region, but we can add region overrides later if needed.

2025-03-13 (Rina Kobayashi): Addressed race where state machine could set Ready on Validating completion while canary callback was still in-flight. Fix merged as part of gating changes (see PR-48245 reference in parent issue).
2025-03-14 (Vanessa Ortiz): Marking Done. Follow-up created to tighten thresholds after we collect 10+ successful runs per SKU and to add region override support if needed.
